title: A state machine of compareAndSet transitions

blocks.text: The page's second pitfall is a state machine with many intermediate states, nested locks and complex transition rules. Its fix: keep the states few, and make each transition one `compareAndSet` on an `AtomicReference`:

Write `Job`, whose nested `enum State` is `IDLE`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, and which starts `IDLE`. Each transition returns `true` when it happened, and **`false`, with the state left as it was, when the job is not in the state the transition starts from**:

items: `start()`: `IDLE` to `RUNNING` only, so a second `start()` is refused, and so is a `start()` on a `COMPLETED` or `FAILED` job, which must be reset first;
`complete()`: `RUNNING` to `COMPLETED` only, so it is refused on an `IDLE`, `FAILED` or already `COMPLETED` job;
`fail()`: `RUNNING` to `FAILED` only, refused likewise on `IDLE`, `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`;
`reset()`: `COMPLETED` or `FAILED` back to `IDLE`, and from nowhere else;

blocks.text: Example: a new job's `complete()` is `false` and it stays `IDLE`; `start()` then `complete()` then `reset()` are all `true`, and the job is `IDLE` again.

Making each transition one `compareAndSet`, rather than a `get()` followed by a `set()`, is what keeps it correct when two threads race for the same transition. A race cannot be forced from a test, so that part is this page's quiz; the tests here check the transitions.

cases.says: IDLE, RUNNING, COMPLETED and back; and IDLE, RUNNING, FAILED and back.
start() on a RUNNING, COMPLETED or FAILED job is false and changes nothing.
complete() and fail() on an IDLE, FAILED or COMPLETED job are false and change nothing.
reset() on an IDLE or RUNNING job is false and changes nothing.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A small state machine is kept simple with an AtomicReference whose compareAndSet allows only the legal transitions.
